name: Platt's Lane Estates – 624–638 Platt's Lane
summary: Four staggered pairs of two-storey red-brick townhouses have east-facing paired doors under broad shallow hoods. They feature pale gable ends, rear patios, and vertical siding under windows.

evidence.note: The City of London address layer places 8 individual two-storey homes on this footprint, in the even-numbered range shown in the name.
Western Housing identifies the estate’s 1976 townhouses and publishes the ground and upper floor plans.
4 staggered sections of brown pitched roof are legible in the 2025 orthophoto. The paved approach is beside walls 6, 7, 8, 10. The roof colour is sampled from the unlabelled orthophoto.
Regional 2 m lidar above local ground measures 6.57 m at P50, 6.96 m at P90 and 7.15 m at maximum. The clear townhouse rows put the ridge near 7 m and the lower eaves near 5.6 m.
Four entrance groups beside the sidewalk, each with a broad shared hood between the window stacks. Pale masonry ends project above the shingles.
White paired casements, vertical brown infill under the upper window, running-bond brick, paired white single doors and a pitched hood.
Sunlit rear beyond the trees shows fenced patios, light-trimmed windows and warm brown wall panels. Used for daylight colour comparison.
Oblique north approach gives the shallow roof pitch and blank pale end plane.

Colour references for the estate are the sunlit rear brick in frame 130394381 and the front brick in 46920592. The palette allows for the warm direct sun on the rear and shade on the front. At 1050 × 590 the rear brick mean at (582,404)–(605,418) is RGB 225,168,113. At 1000 × 550 the shaded front brick at (344,214)–(362,222) is RGB 108,65,60. The specified brick lies between these lighting conditions.

The wider and narrower estate plans show mirrored living-room windows and independent front doors. Each unit has a separate door to the rear patio. The frontage width is used to choose the closest available plan.
The roof and rear screen divisions were registered against the 2025 orthophoto and metre-grid lidar. The individual rear terraces lie outside the eaves. Board finish is inferred on obscured terraces.
Estate frame 130394349 shows a stepped darker stucco field and lighter gable on windowless terminal walls. The same treatment is inferred on concealed ends.
21 small exhaust caps were located by their contrasting highlights and shadows immediately beside the roof ridge. The short concrete entry walks follow visible strips in the orthophoto.

notes: A light cap follows the ridge and both slopes of the tan crosswalls. Each pair shares one shingled hood. Vertical boards connect the window heads and sills. The rear elevations have patio sliders and timber divisions. Their positions on obscured elevations follow the nearest estate floor plan.
